news.title: Protect your enterprise now from the Shai-Hulud worm and npm vulnerability in 6 actionable steps
news.summary_raw: Any development environment that installed or imported one of the 172 compromised npm or PyPI packages published since May 11 should be treated as potentially compromised. On affected developer workstations, the worm harvests credentials from over 100 file paths: AWS keys, SSH private keys, npm tokens, GitHub PATs, HashiCorp Vault tokens, Kubernetes service accounts, Docker configs, shell history, and cryptocurrency wallets. For the first time in a TeamPCP campaign, it targets password managers
news.summary: A Shai-Hulud worm, targeting AWS keys, SSH private keys, and other sensitive files, has been discovered in compromised npm or PyPI packages, and developers should treat affected workstations as compromised. This worm targets various sensitive files, including password managers, and can lead to a security breach.
news.enterprise_use: Check your development environment, identify and update all installed packages, review file paths, and flag any compromised workstations to prevent a potential security breach in your enterprise.

news.title: mimalloc: A new, high-performance, scalable memory allocator for the modern era
news.summary_raw:
mimalloc is an open-source, modern, scalable memory allocator that is a drop-in replacement for malloc and free. It is relatively small (~12K lines), with clear internal data structures, and is easy to build and integrate into other projects. It provides bounded worst-case allocation times (up to OS primitives), bounded space overhead, low internal fragmentation, and minimal contention by relying almost exclusively on atomic operations.
The post mimalloc: A new, high-performance, scalable memory
news.summary: Microsoft Research released mimalloc, a high-performance memory allocator that is a drop-in replacement for malloc and free.
